paths.name: From idea to market
paths.label: The startup path
paths.headline: Ship a product. Not a platform project.
paths.description: For founders and small engineering teams turning a promising idea into a product customers can buy. Start with the commercial picture, then make deliberate build, data, and delivery choices.
paths.outcome: Leave with a product architecture, a faster delivery loop, and a route to market.

steps.why: Start with product differentiation and distribution, not a shopping list of services. This session connects AI product development to Microsoft Marketplace and commercial programs.
steps.takeaway: Map one product differentiator and one viable route to your first or next customers.

steps.why: Compare App Service, Container Apps, and Functions before taking on infrastructure work. A small team needs a runtime that can ship quickly without abandoning production controls.
steps.takeaway: Choose a candidate runtime and write down the operational work it removes.

steps.why: Watch a feature move from prompt to merged pull request using parallel coding agents. Focus on the review and validation steps that keep a small team in control.
steps.takeaway: Pick one repeatable development task to automate, with a named human review gate.

steps.why: If AI is part of your product, state and retrieval are product decisions. Learn how operational data, agent memory, and search fit together before building separate systems for each.
steps.takeaway: Sketch where application state, conversation history, and retrieval data will live.

steps.why: A fast CI pipeline is also a path to your credentials and production systems. Take practical GitHub Actions defenses into your delivery process before customer trust depends on it.
steps.takeaway: Audit workflow permissions, action pinning, and the trust boundary for pull requests.

steps.why: Agent-assisted development has an operating cost. Learn how model choices, workflows, Actions, and adoption reports affect your GitHub Copilot investment; this is not a general Azure FinOps session.
steps.takeaway: Set a Copilot spending budget and define an adoption metric worth tracking.

paths.name: Build an AI-native product
paths.label: The AI product path
paths.headline: Get beyond the impressive demo.
paths.description: For teams putting agents into a customer-facing product. Make the architecture decision first, then connect knowledge, measure quality, and earn the right to scale.
paths.outcome: Leave with an agent architecture and a measurable path from prototype to production.

steps.why: Choose between prompt agents, a managed harness, and hosted agents before committing to a framework. Match ownership and control to your product, not the most elaborate demo.
steps.takeaway: Document your build-versus-managed choice and one condition that would change it.

steps.why: Connect local development, hosted deployment, tools, grounding, and evaluation into one picture. Use that picture to identify your smallest useful agent release.
steps.takeaway: Outline a thin vertical slice from a user request to a measurable result.

steps.why: See the retrieval loop built by hand before comparing it with Foundry IQ. Understanding the plumbing makes the managed-service tradeoff a deliberate choice.
steps.takeaway: Choose a retrieval approach and name the evidence your agent must cite.

steps.why: Traces, evaluations, and optimization turn vague feedback into a repeatable improvement loop. Establish quality and cost signals before expanding usage.
steps.takeaway: Define a small evaluation set, a quality threshold, and a cost metric.

steps.why: An agent running code needs more than a capable model. Examine isolation, identity, governance, and observability with Container Apps sandboxes before trusting it with real work.
steps.takeaway: List the permissions, isolation boundary, and telemetry required for each tool.

steps.why: Once one agent works, the challenge becomes operating many of them. Bring AI Gateway, identity, responsible AI controls, and FinOps into the scaling plan.
steps.takeaway: Assign owners for agent identity, usage budgets, policy, and production incidents.

paths.name: Scale without the sprawl
paths.label: The digital-native path
paths.headline: Grow the business. Not the operational burden.
paths.description: For digital-native companies with production customers and growing platforms. Follow the operating model from architecture and fleet management to data, observability, and secure delivery.
paths.outcome: Leave with a focused platform backlog for resilience, security, and lower operational toil.

steps.why: Use Microsoft's own AI workload practices as a reference, not a blueprint to copy wholesale. Identify which architecture, reliability, and governance lessons fit your current scale.
steps.takeaway: Name your biggest production constraint and one practice worth adapting.

steps.why: If you already operate Kubernetes across environments, examine fleet management before multiplying bespoke clusters. This is a scale-out session, not a reason to adopt Kubernetes from scratch.
steps.takeaway: Identify one fleet-wide policy and one repeated operation to standardize.

steps.why: Explore PostgreSQL fleet management, compute, storage, and immutable backups through production lessons. Prioritize this step if PostgreSQL is part of your stack.
steps.takeaway: Review your recovery objectives and one database performance or cost bottleneck.

steps.why: Connect infrastructure, application, and AI-agent observability instead of adding another isolated dashboard. Start with the signals that shorten investigations for your team.
steps.takeaway: Map a critical user journey to the health signals needed to diagnose it.

steps.why: Platform scale amplifies the blast radius of CI mistakes. Use concrete GitHub Actions attack paths to tighten credentials, workflow trust, and action dependencies.
steps.takeaway: Create a prioritized workflow-hardening backlog with an accountable owner.

steps.why: Explore an AI SRE teammate only after the platform has useful telemetry and clear operational boundaries. Look for repetitive investigations, not reasons to remove human accountability.
steps.takeaway: Choose one low-risk operational workflow with an approval and rollback plan.
